forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson or Foreign Minister Araghchi issues a formal public statement — via IRNA, MFA press conference, or state-broadcast — listing specific named conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, before EOD 2026-09-02.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IRNA or official MFA transcript plus one TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP) carrying the statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: SNSC officials or IRGC spokespeople speaking to media without MFA imprimatur = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. A list from 'informed sources' without formal MFA attribution = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Restatements of existing general positions without a new enumerated list = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

Iran's IRGC responded with approximately 32 ballistic missiles targeting US military installations at King Hussein Air Base and Al-Azraq base, Jordan, on 2026-08-31, confirmed by Gulf News, Jerusalem Post, and ANI News. Ceasefire ended Day 184 (2026-08-30). RESOLVED-NO.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if no TIER1-confirmed US/Israeli strike on Iranian sovereign territory AND no Iranian missile/drone strike on Israeli territory or US regional military bases occurs from 2026-08-30 through EOD 2026-09-30. forecasts.question: Will Eisenkot (or a Yashar-led nominee) be sworn in as Israeli Prime Minister heading a coalition government before EOD 2027-01-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: No material movement — pre-election cadence holds. Channel 12 late-August polling gives Yashar 24 seats vs. Likud's 22; Eisenkot leads Netanyahu on PM suitability by 14 percentage points, the widest gap since Yashar's founding. Oct 27 election date is firm following Knesset dissolution Jul 17. Coalition arithmetic to 61 seats requires Yashar to secure partners from religious, centrist, and/or Arab-list blocs; no Haredi bloc commitment is on record for either Netanyahu or Eisenkot. Coalition math is the dominant variable and cannot be resolved until post-election negotiations begin.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Eisenkot or a Yashar-led nominee is formally sworn in as Prime Minister before the President of Israel following an Oct 27, 2026 election, heading a coalition government, before EOD 2027-01-15.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-YES (DA hygiene audit, Day 185). The Knesset's unanimous self-dissolution (62-0 vote) on 2026-07-17 satisfies the resolution criteria under the natural textual reading: 'dissolution with date earlier than 2026-10-27.' The dissolution event date (July 17, 2026) is earlier than the Oct 27 threshold. This meets both the spirit and the most natural textual reading of the criteria. The forecast was incorrectly retained at p=0.10 following Sunday's cold-start audit; the weekly-cadence hold rule does not apply when the outcome is factually complete and no longer uncertain. Retired as RESOLVED-YES. Lesson: future 'early dissolution' resolution criteria should specify dissolution event date vs. election date explicitly.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution with the dissolution date occurring earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas for the original forecast — but retirement applies whenever outcome is factually complete.
